title: Curve rate limits drop their unit suffix, leaving the denomination ambiguous for a two-asset pool
content:
Lending instances always name the unit: "`maxAmount`: 100,000,000 USDC", "`slope`: 50,000,000 DAI per day". Every Curve instance drops it. The sUSDS/USDT pool reads "`maxAmount`: 5,000,000, `slope`: 20,000,000 per day" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.7.1.2.4.1); pyUSD/USDS reads "`maxAmount`: 5,000,000, `slope`: 50,000,000 per day" (.7.4.2.4.1); the weETH/WETH-ng swap limit reads "`maxAmount`: 1,000, `slope`: 50,000 per day" (.7.5.2.4.3).

For the dollar pools the omission is recoverable by assumption. For weETH/WETH-ng it is not merely stylistic: 1,000 of something with a 50,000 per day refill is obviously ETH-denominated rather than dollar-denominated, but the document never says so, and the pool's two legs — weETH and WETH — are not the same asset even though they trade near parity.

The deeper problem is structural rather than cosmetic. A swap has an input asset and an output asset. A limit of 5,000,000 on a pyUSD/USDC pool could bind the pyUSD side, the USDC side, or whichever asset is being sold, and the three readings give different exposures once the pair dislocates — precisely the state in which the limit matters most.

Because the Curve instances also defer their RateLimitIDs to a future iteration, there is no on-chain key to resolve the ambiguity against. The unit is knowable only from the implementation, which means these particular numbers cannot be verified from the Artifact alone in the way the SparkLend figures can.
description: Where SparkLend writes 100,000,000 USDC, Curve instances write bare figures like maxAmount 5,000,000
